title: Archive the Day's Triage
subtitle: Retain it and seed the taxonomy loop
scenario: The digest is sent. Close the day by archiving the triage: retain the records and digest for audit, and mark that it seeds the taxonomy loop. Yesterday's misroutes are what tune tomorrow's categories.
input: Today's triage is complete: 3 tickets, digest assembled. Archive it under archive id triage-day-1 with a 1-year retention. Mark seedsTaxonomy true - the day's misroutes feed the taxonomy-feedback step.
instructions: Record the archive id and the ticket count.
Mark that it seeds the taxonomy (seedsTaxonomy).
Return one valid JSON object, then validate.
copilotPrompt: Build one JSON triage archive record: archiveId triage-day-1, ticketCount 3, retention 1 year, seedsTaxonomy true.
successMessage: Triage archived. It is retained for audit and marked to seed the taxonomy loop.
editorHelper: Retain the day - and mark that it feeds the taxonomy.

intro.heading: Close the day: retain and seed

sections.title: Retention is a compliance decision
sections.body: The day's triage is kept for a defined period so an auditor can reconstruct what was routed where. The retention length is a governed choice, not an afterthought.

sections.title: The archive feeds the loop
sections.body: This archive is not a dead end. Its misroutes flow to the taxonomy-feedback step: a category that keeps getting reworked becomes a change proposal. Yesterday tunes tomorrow.

sections.title: A stable id
sections.body: The day is archived under a stable id so it can be found again. A weak id makes the archive unsearchable and the loop impossible.

sections.title: What you produce here
sections.body: An archive record that satisfies retention and opens the temporal loop back to the taxonomy.

takeaway.heading: Triage archived
points: You retained the day's triage under a stable id.
The archive is marked to seed the taxonomy - a loop input.
Retention keeps the day findable for audit and learning.
The day's misroutes now flow to the taxonomy-feedback step.
The workflow can now retain each day and feed it back to the taxonomy.
